answer:
Chandrayaan-3’s standout scientific result was the first in-situ detection and measurement of sulfur on the Moon’s south-polar surface, made by the Pragyan rover. It also measured other elements, helping scientists characterize the local lunar soil and showing that sulfur could be mapped directly at the landing site. [1]

The mission additionally made the first measurements of the near-surface lunar plasma environment in the south-polar region, finding it relatively sparse.
